content:
The account chip lives in `src/components/Navigation.tsx`. The same `UserChip` (photo, username and #id) shows in three places: the desktop bar (line 116), the mobile top bar (line 124) and the header of the mobile slide-in menu (line 149). The comment on line 122 says a `hide-sm` class collapses the chip to just the photo on mobile. The owner still sees the full chip on small screens, so that class probably kicks in at a narrower width than the `md` point where the mobile layout starts; I haven't checked the CSS to confirm. The fix is one file: give the chip a compact, photo-only mode for the two mobile spots, or fix the breakpoint.

I rated it **standard / sonnet** rather than trivial / haiku. Trivial means no logic branches, and this needs a photo-only variant plus working out why `hide-sm` isn't applying. The menu does animate, but that animation stays as it is, so the motion override (which sends motion work to opus) doesn't apply. It's one frontend area with low risk, so no design round. `RETRO.md` has no parked tasks yet, and I didn't add a close-call entry to `DECISIONS.md`.
